newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crude grade prices gain on refiner plays.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crude grade prices gain on refiner plays.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes gained ground Tuesday morning in-line with technical buying in the NYMEX futures market, while grade barrels popped higher on increased refiner purchases.

July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was around 30 cents higher at $19.35-45 a barrel, holding around a 10 cents premium to the futures board on the Exchange for Physicals (EFPs) premium, traders said.
"Refiners have been short all month, so now they've come back in to buy their ratable barrels that they had delayed doing," said a cash trader.
Dealers said Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James had improved to talk at a five cents discount to flat against the cash WTI benchmark, seven cents stronger than Monday.
West Texas Sour/Midland also moved to close the discount held to the benchmark, talking Tuesday morning at $1.40 under, 10 cents firmer than late Monday.

July EFPs remained at eight cents over paper values, steady from deals recorded yesterday. Traders said indications that a U.S. refiner took delivery of a large portion of Nigerian Bonny Light -- absorbing foreign overhang -- had pressured EFPs. But, the premium remained stuck at current levels on thoguhts the Bonny Light buyer may redeliver the crude against July NYMEX futures contracts.
"The talk of 4 million barrels being taken is a lot of sweet crude, especially if you want to store it," said a cash trader.
